Entries.Text: Find dummies, materials, bones, meshes and model headers with a filter, then edit or delete every match at once. Find on the first tab; preview and apply on the second.
Edit or delete the objects found, with a preview of every change.
Where the objects are looked for.
The objects selected in the loaded model. Selecting the model root picks its header.
Every object of the loaded model.
Every model of the loaded model's file, such as a part or DS2 map binder holding several.
Every model of the project, or of one Source List list. Each file is read, so it can take a while.
Load a model to use this scope.
Select a dummy, material, bone, mesh or the model root first.
Matches the model name, the name of its file, or its alias. Empty for every model in the scope.
The kind of object, and its name: a bone or material by name, a dummy by reference ID, a mesh by position. With Any, the text also matches the kind.
Each condition must be met by one of the object's fields. Empty conditions are ignored.
The field the value must be in, by its path (Textures[0].Path, BoundingBox.Min) or part of it. Empty for any field.
Adds a condition. Every condition must be met.
How the text inputs are matched.
Find the objects, or start over.
Finds every object the filter matches. Nothing is changed until Apply on the Edit tab.
The objects the edit applies to. Click one to jump to it.
The filter or the scope's selection has changed since Find. Find again to edit what it asks for now.
Find the objects to edit on the Find tab first.
Models that aren't loaded are edited directly: those edits can't be undone, and are written with Save All.
What to do to the matches.
Each step sets a field. Steps run in order, each on the value the step before it left. An object that a step can't be applied to is left wholly alone.
The field to set. Only fields that can be set are listed, from the objects found.
Adds a step, run after the others.
The value the operator uses. Numbers use a dot for decimals.
Sets the value. A vector takes one number per component.
Adds to the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Subtracts from the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Multiplies the value. A vector takes one number for every component, or one per component.
Divides the value. Dividing by zero skips the object.
Raises the value to the number given, if it is lower.
Lowers the value to the number given, if it is higher.
Flips the value: true becomes false, false becomes true.
Replaces every occurrence of the text, ignoring case, such as part of a texture path.
Every change Apply will make, worked out from the steps. Click one to jump to its object.
Pick a field in a step to see the changes.
The matches are out of date. Find again before applying.
Makes every change listed. A loaded model's changes are one undo step; models that aren't loaded are left unsaved.
Replace needs the text to find
The operator doesn't apply to this field
{0} is kept with its history in a view: load it to edit it.
Bone links can only be changed in a loaded model, which keeps the hierarchy in step.
A model header can't be deleted.
Objects can only be deleted from loaded models.
{0} objects had changed or gone since Find and were left alone.
{0} models that aren't loaded were changed and are unsaved. Use {1} to write them.
Find again to make another edit.
Mass edit: applied to {0} objects, {1} stale, {2} skipped.
The objects Delete removes. Click one to jump to it.
Only objects of loaded models are deleted, as one undo step in each view. Indices that point at deleted bones and materials are updated, as deleting in Contents does.
Deletes every match of a loaded model.
Delete {0} objects? Bones take their child bones with them. Undo puts them back.
Mass edit: deleted {0} objects, {1} stale, {2} skipped.
Fills in the Mass Edit filter from this search and finds the objects there, so they can be edited or deleted all at once.
